questions.stem: A 35-year-old male patient with a history of chronic pain is being managed on an oral pain medication. The healthcare team is monitoring the patient's response to medication and decides to take periodic plasma concentration samples. The team wants to evaluate the rate at which the drug is absorbed into the patient's system. Which of the following parameters on a plasma concentration vs. time graph would be most indicative of the rate of drug absorption for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
2.0pt;">Ans. D. Tmax

 

Explanation of Options:

 

A) Area under the Curve (AUC): This parameter reflects the total drug exposure over time but does not give insights into the rate of drug absorption.

 

B) Half-life (T1/2): This measures how long it takes for the drug concentration to decrease to half its initial value, more related to the elimination phase rather than the absorption rate.

 

C) Maximum concentration (Cmax): This indicates the peak concentration of the drug in the bloodstream but doesn't specify how quickly this level is reached.

 

D) Time to reach maximum concentration (Tmax): This is the time it takes for the drug to reach its peak concentration in the plasma. It gives an indication of how quickly the drug is absorbed into the system.

 

Therefore, the time to reach maximum concentration (Tmax) is the best parameter to evaluate the rate of drug absorption.

questions.stem: Adrenaline acting via beta 2 receptors causes bronchodilation whereas histamine acting through H1 receptors cause bronchoconstriction. Which type of antagonism it is?
questions.solutionHtml:
strong>Ans. D. Physiological Antagonism

 

Explanation of Options:

 

A) Pharmacological Antagonism: This term generally refers to one drug reducing the effectiveness of another drug, typically through receptor competition or a similar mechanism at the molecular level. Since adrenaline and histamine act on different receptors to produce opposite physiological effects, this option is not correct.

 

B) Chemical Antagonism: This occurs when one drug directly reacts with another to neutralize its effects e.g. antacids neutralize gastric acid and protamine neutralize heparin. There is no direct chemical reaction between adrenaline and histamine, making this option incorrect.

 

C) Physical Antagonism: This would imply that the drugs physically interfere with each other e.g. charcoal adbsorbs many drugs and is used in drug poisoning.

 

D) Physiological Antagonism: This is the correct answer. Physiological antagonism occurs when two drugs produce opposite effects in the same physiological system. Adrenaline causes bronchodilation via beta-2 receptors, while histamine causes bronchoconstriction via H1 receptors. These drugs act on different receptor types but have opposite effects on the same physiological system, namely the bronchial smooth muscle.

questions.stem: A farmer presents to the emergency department with pinpoint pupil, diarrhea, sweating, excessive lacrimation, salivation and muscle weakness. On examination there is bradycardia and BP is 80/60 mm Hg pulse rate is 56/min and his plasma cholinesterase level was 52 U/mL. Which of the following drugs can be used for treatment of muscle weakness in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
lanation of Options:

 

A) Pralidoxine: This drug is typically used alongside atropine for treating organophosphate poisoning to reactivate acetylcholinesterase. It can reverse muscle weakness. 

 

B) Atropine: Atropine acts as an antagonist at muscarinic cholinergic receptors and would counteract many of the symptoms observed like pinpoint pupils, excessive salivation, and bradycardia. However it cannot reverse muscle weakness.

 

C) Physostigmine: This drug is a cholinesterase inhibitor and would worsen the symptoms of cholinergic toxicity, making it an inappropriate treatment in this case.

 

D) N-acetylcysteine: This is commonly used for acetaminophen overdose and would not be effective for treating symptoms of cholinergic toxicity.

questions.stem: A 55-year-old male patient with chronic gout is under consideration for a change in treatment plan due to poor response to conventional therapies like allopurinol and colchicine. The healthcare team is discussing the potential use of rasburicase. What is the mechanism of action of rasburicase?

options.label: B
options.text: Conversion of uric acid to allantoin

questions.answerText: Conversion of uric acid to allantoin
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Conversion of uric acid to allantoin.

 

Option A. Inhibition of xanthine oxidase: This is the mechanism of action for allopurinol, not pegloticase. Allopurinol inhibits xanthine oxidase, which is an enzyme involved in the conversion of hypoxanthine and xanthine to uric acid.

 

Option B. Conversion of uric acid to allantoin: Rasburicase is a recombinant uricase enzyme that converts uric acid into allantoin, which is more soluble and easier to excrete through the kidneys. This action helps to lower high levels of uric acid in patients with chronic gout.

 

Option C. Increase excretion of uric acid: Some medications like probenecid work by this mechanism to increase the renal excretion of uric acid.

 

Option D. Inhibition of granulocyte migration: Colchicine works through inhibiting granulocyte migration, but pegloticase primarily works by metabolizing uric acid.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man with a history of benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) is scheduled to receive a new medication. The physician explains the mechanism of action and potential side effects of dutasteride to the patient and his family. Which of the following is true about finasteride?

options.label: A
options.text: It increases the production of testosterone.

options.label: B
options.text: It act as an antagonist of androgen receptors.

options.label: C
options.text: It can cause sexual side effects such as decreased libido and erectile dysfunction.

options.label: D
options.text: It is only effective in reducing symptoms of BPH in the short-term.

questions.answerText: It can cause sexual side effects such as decreased libido and erectile dysfunction.
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) It can cause sexual side effects such as decreased libido and erectile dysfunction.

 

  • Finasteride like drugs are a class of medications used to treat BPH by reducing the size of the prostate gland.
  • They work by inhibiting the enzyme 5 alpha reductase, which converts testosterone to dihydrotestosterone (DHT). 
  • By reducing the levels of DHT, 5 alpha reductase inhibitors can shrink the prostate gland and improve urinary symptoms associated with BPH. 
  • A potential side effect of these medications is sexual dysfunction, including decreased libido and erectile dysfunction. 
  • These medications can take several months to achieve their maximum effect and can provide long-term relief of BPH symptoms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a correct match with respect to the mechanism of action and clinical use of the given drugs?

options.label: A
options.text: Zavegepant - CGRP receptor antagonist used for the treatment of acute migraine attacks

options.label: B
options.text: Pembrolizumab – Immune check point inhibitor used for endometrial carcinoma

options.label: C
options.text: Ertugliflozin – SGLT2 inhibitor for treatment of diabetes mellitus

options.label: D
options.text: Ivabradine – Funny current blocker for treatment of decreased visual acuity

questions.answerText: Ivabradine – Funny current blocker for treatment of decreased visual acuity
questions.solutionHtml:
r treatment of decreased visual acuity.

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Zavegepant - CGRP receptor antagonist used for the treatment of acute migraine attacks: This is a correct match. Zavegepant is a calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) receptor antagonist. It is used for the treatment of acute migraine attacks. CGRP is a neuropeptide that plays a role in the pathophysiology of migraines, and antagonists like Zavegepant block its activity, thereby alleviating symptoms.

 

B) Pembrolizumab – Immune check point inhibitor used for endometrial carcinoma: This is also a correct match. Pembrolizumab is an immune checkpoint inhibitor that targets the PD-1 receptor. It is used for a variety of cancers, including endometrial carcinoma, especially in cases that are MSI-H or dMMR (microsatellite instability-high or mismatch repair deficient).

 

C) Ertugliflozin – SGLT2 inhibitor for treatment of diabetes mellitus: This is another correct match. Ertugliflozin is a Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor, which is used to manage blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes mellitus. It works by inhibiting the reabsorption of glucose in the kidneys, thereby leading to the excretion of glucose in the urine.

 

D) Ivabradine – Funny current blocker for treatment of decreased visual acuity: This is the incorrect match. Ivabradine is indeed a "funny" current (If) blocker, but it is used for the treatment of certain types of chronic heart failure and angina pectoris (chest pain), not for treating decreased visual acuity.

 

Therefore, option D is not a correct match concerning the mechanism of action and clinical use of the given drug.

questions.stemHtml: In a dog blood pressure experiment, a researcher injected phentolamine first followed by epinephrine and the recordings of the effect are shown in the diagram given below. This phenomenon is known as?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Vasomotor reversal of Dale

 

  • Normally epinephrine produces a biphasic response on blood pressure which is characterized by increase in BP followed by decrease in BP. First increase is due to stimulation of alpha 1 receptors and later on decrease is due to stimulation of beta 2 receptors.
  • However, If alpha blockers like phentolamine are already given and then we administer epinephrine, it causes only exaggerated fall in blood pressure. This is called vasomotor reversal of Dale.
  • If we give same dose of a drug repeatedly and there is decrease in effect of the drug, it is called tachyphylaxis. It is shown by drugs like ephedrine.
  • There is no term like phentolamine epinephrine coupling.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old researcher is studying a novel antiviral drug that has shown promise in in-vitro studies. The researcher is in the process of planning the clinical development of the drug. She explains to her team that the next step involves a phase zero clinical trial, which will be crucial in determining whether to move on to phase I trials. The team is confused, as they are not familiar with phase zero clinical trials. Which of the following statements is true regarding phase zero clinical trials, that would help the team understand its significance?

options.label: A
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials are typically conducted in animal models to assess the safety and efficacy of a new drug.

options.label: B
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials are comprehensive studies designed to provide conclusive data on the safety and efficacy of a new drug.

options.label: C
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials primarily focus on pharmacokinetics, particularly on the movement of the drug in the human body.

options.label: D
options.text: Phase zero clinical trials are also known as therapeutic trials and aim to cure or mitigate symptoms of the disease in question.

questions.answerText: Phase zero clinical trials primarily focus on pharmacokinetics, particularly on the movement of the drug in the human body.
questions.solutionHtml:
Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Phase zero clinical trials are typically conducted in animal models to assess the safety and efficacy of a new drug: This statement is incorrect. Phase zero clinical trials are human trials that precede phase I trials. They are not animal studies.

 

B) Phase zero clinical trials are comprehensive studies designed to provide conclusive data on the safety and efficacy of a new drug: This is incorrect. Phase zero trials are not designed to provide comprehensive data on safety and efficacy but are focused on pharmacokinetics and perhaps some initial pharmacodynamic data.

 

C) Phase zero clinical trials primarily focus on pharmacokinetics, particularly on the movement of the drug in the human body: This is correct. The main aim of phase zero trials is to gather preliminary data on pharmacokinetics and assess whether the drug behaves in humans as it does in preclinical models.

 

D) Phase zero clinical trials are also known as therapeutic trials and aim to cure or mitigate symptoms of the disease in question: This is incorrect. Phase zero trials are exploratory trials that precede phase I trials; they are not focused on therapeutic outcomes.

 

Therefore, the statement that would best help the team understand the significance of phase zero trials is that they primarily focus on pharmacokinetics and provide initial human data on the movement and metabolism of the drug.

questions.stem: A 60-year-old female with a history of glaucoma presents to the ophthalmologist with complaints of blurred vision and eye irritation. The patient reports that she has been using an anti-glaucoma medication for the past six months, and her symptoms began to appear gradually over the past few weeks. Upon further evaluation, it is discovered that the patient has experienced darkening of the iris and eyelid skin as well as increased length, thickness, and pigmentation of the eyelashes. Which of the following anti-glaucoma drugs is likely to produce these adverse effects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Latanoprost.

  • The patient's symptoms are consistent with the known side effects of latanoprost, which is a prostaglandin analog used in the treatment of glaucoma.
  • Latanoprost can cause:
    • Pigmentation of Iris: It is also known as heterochromia iridis
    • Growth of Eyelashes: It is also called hypertrichosis
    • Macular Edema
    • Worsening of inflammation: So contraindicated in patients with uveitis.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male with a history of chronic kidney disease presents to the emergency department with complaints of muscle weakness, nausea, and abdominal cramping. Laboratory testing shows that the patient has hyperkalemia, with a serum potassium level of 6.5 mEq/L. The patient's medications are reviewed, and it is discovered that he has been taking several drugs for his cardiac conditions and hypertension. Upon further evaluation, it is determined that one of these drugs may be contributing to the patient's hyperkalemia. Which of the following drugs should be stopped in this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Enalapril

  • Enalapril is an ACE inhibitor used in the treatment of hypertension and can cause hyperkalemia as a side effect.
  • Hydrochlorothiazide is a thiazide diuretic and Furosemide is a loop diuretic, these can cause hypokalemia but not hyperkalemia.
  • Amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker that does not typically cause electrolyte imbalances.

questions.stem: A 70-year-old male patient with a history of heart failure and atrial fibrillation has been taking digoxin for several months. He was recently started on a new medication for hypertension. He presents to the clinic with symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and visual disturbances. Which of the following drugs is most likely responsible for these symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Hydrochlorothiazide

  • Symptoms of digoxin toxicity include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, and visual disturbances. Other symptoms can include dizziness, confusion, and changes in heart rate or rhythm. Hydrochlorothiazide can cause electrolyte abnormalities such as hypokalaemia, which can increase the risk of digoxin toxicity.
  • Metformin is an oral antidiabetic medication that does not interact with digoxin.
  • Lisinopril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor and amlodipine is a calcium channel blocker, both of which do not interact with digoxin.

questions.stem: A 65-year-old male presents with symptoms of urinary urgency, frequency, and nocturia. He has been diagnosed with overactive bladder and his previous medication (oxybutynin) was not effective in managing his symptoms. Which of the following drugs is a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist that may be effective in treating this patient's symptoms?
questions.solutionHtml:
Calibri,sans-serif">Ans. C. Vibegron

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

A) Tolterodine: This drug is an antimuscarinic agent, not a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist. It is commonly used in the treatment of overactive bladder but works through a different mechanism of action than beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonists.

 

B) Memantine: Memantine is an NMDA receptor antagonist used primarily in the treatment of moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease. It has no role in the treatment of overactive bladder.

 

C) Vibegron: This is a beta-3 adrenergic receptor agonist (similar to mirabegron) that is used in the treatment of overactive bladder. By stimulating beta-3 adrenergic receptors in the detrusor muscle of the bladder, it relaxes the muscle and improves symptoms like urinary urgency and frequency.

 

D) Levetiracetam: Levetiracetam is an antiepileptic drug that is used to treat various types of seizures. It has no role in the treatment of overactive bladder.

questions.stemHtml: Given image shows the Log DRC of a drug alone (A) and in the presence of antagonists (B and C). Identify the type of antagonism shown in curve B and curve C?

options.label: A
options.text: B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist

options.label: B
options.text: B is non-competitive an C is competitive antagonist

questions.answerText: B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist
questions.solutionHtml:
a non-competitive antagonist.

 

Explanation of options:

 

A. B is competitive and C is non-competitive antagonist: This is the correct answer. B shows a parallel shift to the right, which is characteristic of competitive antagonism. Increasing the concentration of the agonist can overcome the antagonist. C shows a reduction in the maximal response that the agonist can produce, characteristic of a non-competitive antagonist.

 

B. B is non-competitive and C is competitive antagonist: This is incorrect. B shows a parallel shift to the right, which is indicative of competitive antagonism. C shows a reduction in the maximal response, which is indicative of non-competitive antagonism.

 

C. Both are competitive antagonists: This is incorrect. Curve B shows characteristics of competitive antagonism, but curve C shows characteristics of non-competitive antagonism as it reduces the maximal response of the agonist.

 

D. Both are non-competitive antagonists: This is incorrect. Curve B shows characteristics of competitive antagonism as it shifts parallel to the right, while curve C shows characteristics of non-competitive antagonism as it reduces the maximal response of the agonist.

questions.stemHtml: What does IP in the figure shown stands for:

options.label: A
options.text: Drug is an instant release preparation

options.label: C
options.text: The standards according to Indian Pharmacopoeia

options.label: D
options.text: Drug tested preclinically via Intraperitoneal route

questions.answerText: The standards according to Indian Pharmacopoeia
questions.solutionHtml:
Pharmacopoeia

 

Explanation of all the options:

 

a. Drug is an instant release preparation: The term "IP" on a drug strip doesn't typically signify that the drug is an instant release preparation. This would usually be denoted by terms like "IR" rather than "IP."

 

b. Meant for intra pulmonary use: The abbreviation "IP" is not commonly used to denote that a drug is meant for intrapulmonary use. Instead, you would likely see terms such as "inhaler" or "nebulizer" or specific abbreviations for pulmonary administration.

 

c. The standards according to Indian Pharmacopoeia: This is the correct answer. The term "IP" is often used on pharmaceutical packaging in India to denote that the drug meets the standards laid out in the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

 

d. Drug tested preclinically via IntraPeritoneal route: "IP" is commonly used as an abbreviation for intraperitoneal in scientific research, but it is unlikely to be used in this context on a drug strip meant for patient use.

 

Therefore, the correct interpretation of "IP" on the drug strip of asthalin is that the drug complies with the standards of the Indian Pharmacopoeia.



ore, the correct interpretation of "IP" on the drug strip of asthalin is that the drug complies with the standards of the Indian Pharmacopoeia.

questions.stemHtml: A new antiarrhythmic drug is found to be effective against both atrial and ventricular arrhythmias. Its effect on action potential is shown in the Figure. The effect of this new drug is most similar to?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Procainamide

  • This drug is decreasing the slope of phase 0 (Na+ channel blocking property) as well as increasing the action potential duration (K+ channel blocking property). Thus, it exhibits the properties of class Ia anti-arrhythmic agents.

  • Class Ia anti-arrhythmics include quinidine and procainamide.

  • These drugs can result in QT prolongation in ECG.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A patient is admitted to the emergency department for treatment of a drug overdose. The identity of the drug is unknown, but it is observed that when the urine pH is acidic, the renal clearance of the drug is less than GFR and that when the urine pH is alkaline, the clearance is greater than GFR. The drug probably is?
questions.solutionHtml:
The drug is most likely a weak acid (Choice B).

 

Explanation:

 

When the urine pH is acidic, the renal clearance of a weak acid drug is less than the glomerular filtration rate (GFR). This is because in acidic urine, weak acid drugs remain predominantly in their non-ionized form, which hinders their excretion into the urine. As a result, their renal clearance is limited.

 

On the other hand, when the urine pH is alkaline, the renal clearance of a weak acid drug is greater than the GFR. In alkaline urine, weak acid drugs become ionized, which promotes their excretion into the urine. This leads to a higher renal clearance compared to the GFR.

 

Strong acids (Choice A) and strong bases (Choice D) are usually fully ionized and do not undergo significant changes in their excretion based on urine pH.

 

Therefore, based on the observed changes in renal clearance in response to urine pH, the drug in question is most likely a weak acid (Choice B).



ore, based on the observed changes in renal clearance in response to urine pH, the drug in question is most likely a weak acid (Choice B).

questions.stem: A 43-year-old, insulin-dependent diabetic patient is diagnosed with hypertension and begins therapy with an antihypertensive agent. Three days later, he measures his blood glucose at home and finds that it is 53 mg/dL. He recalibrates his glucose testing apparatus and repeats the test, only to find that the first reading was accurate. He is concerned that his hypoglycemia did not produce the normal premonitory signs and symptoms. Which of the following medications was most likely prescribed to treat his hypertension?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Propranolol

 

  • Propranolol belongs to the class of medications known as beta-blockers. Beta-blockers can mask the typical signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia, such as tachycardia, palpitations and tremors by blocking the beta-adrenergic receptors that are responsible for these responses. As a result, the patient may experience hypoglycemia without being aware of it.
  • In contrast, medications like captopril (A), diltiazem (B), and methyldopa (C) are not known to mask the signs and symptoms of hypoglycemia.
  • Note that beta blockers do not stop sweating as it is mediated by M3 muscarinic receptors.

questions.stem: A young female presented with left sided severe throbbing headache associated with nausea, vomiting, photophobia and phonophobia. Which of the following is a new drug that can provide immediate relief to this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Lasmiditan

  • The symptoms described, including severe throbbing headache, nausea, vomiting, photophobia (sensitivity to light), and phonophobia (sensitivity to sound), are characteristic of a migraine headache.
  • Lasmiditan is a new drug that belongs to a class called 5HT1F agonist. It is specifically approved for the acute treatment of migraine attacks in adults. It provides immediate relief by inhibiting the release of CGRP from the neurons.
  • Other drugs mentioned in the options i.e. Propranolol (choice a), Topiramate (choice c) and  Erenumab (choice d) are used for prophylaxis of migraine and not for treatment of acute attack.
  • Propranolol is DOC for prophylaxis of migraine.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A drug effect that is produced by therapeutic doses of both timolol and amiodarone is blockade of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Beta-adrenoceptors.

  • Both timolol and amiodarone are medications that have a blocking effect on beta-adrenoceptors. Amiodarone is a non-competitive beta blocker whereas drugs ending with lol (like nadolol) are competitive beta blockers.
  • Timolol is a non-selective beta blocker that blocks both beta-1 and beta-2 adrenoceptors.
  • Amiodarone is an antiarrhythmic medication that has actions of all classes of anti-arrhythmic drugs. It is a blocker of Na channels; K channels and Ca channels and it also has non-selective beta-blocking properties.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is wrong about amiodarone?

options.label: A
options.text: It is longest acting anti-arrhythmic drug

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. It has positive ionotropic action

 

  • Amiodarone is a potent antiarrhythmic medication with multiple actions on cardiac ion channels. However, it does not have a positive ionotropic action. In fact, amiodarone has predominantly negative inotropic effects, meaning it reduces the force of cardiac contractions.
  • The correct statements about amiodarone are:
    • It is the longest-acting antiarrhythmic drug: Amiodarone has a half-life of around 3 weeks, meaning it remains in the body for an extended period. This allows for a once-daily dosing regimen in many cases.
    • It contains iodine: Amiodarone contains around 40 percent iodine, which contribute to its structure. This iodine content is responsible for some of the medication's potential adverse effects, such as thyroid abnormalities.
    • It can cause pulmonary fibrosis: Amiodarone has been associated with pulmonary toxicity, which can manifest as lung inflammation and fibrosis.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Mechanism of action of statins is:

options.label: C
options.text: Indirect increase of LDL receptors synthesis

questions.answerText: Indirect increase of LDL receptors synthesis
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Indirect increase of LDL receptor synthesis

 

  • The mechanism of action of statins involves inhibiting HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme responsible for the synthesis of cholesterol in the liver. By inhibiting this enzyme, statins reduce the production of cholesterol in the liver. This leads to indirect increase in the synthesis of LDL receptors in the liver, leading to increased uptake and clearance of LDL cholesterol from the bloodstream. This is the primary mechanism by which statins lower LDL cholesterol levels.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A. Inhibition of HMG-CoA synthase: This is a wrong option as the correct mechanism of action of statins is the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, and not HMG-CoA synthase.

 

Option B. Stimulation of HMG-CoA reductase: This is a wrong option as the correct mechanism of action of statins is the inhibition of HMG-CoA reductase, not the stimulation.

 

Option D. Inhibition of intestinal cholesterol absorption: This is the major mechanism of action of ezetimibe and statins has negligible action in this regard.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Metformin is least likely to reduce blood sugar in which of the following patients?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Non-diabetics

 

  • Metformin is an oral medication commonly used to treat type 2 diabetes. It works by reducing glucose production in the liver, improving insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues, and reducing glucose absorption in the intestines. As a result, metformin helps to lower blood sugar levels in individuals with diabetes.
  • In non-diabetic individuals, who already have normal blood sugar regulation, the use of metformin is not indicated. Metformin does not cause hypoglycemia and since the blood sugar levels of non-diabetics are within the normal range, metformin cannot further reduce blood sugar.
  • The other options listed are more likely to benefit from metformin in terms of blood sugar reduction:

 

A. Obese diabetics: Metformin is commonly prescribed to obese individuals with type 2 diabetes as it helps improve insulin sensitivity and control blood sugar levels.

 

C. Type 2 diabetics: Metformin is considered a first-line treatment for type 2 diabetes and is widely used to reduce blood sugar levels in these patients.

 

D. Diabetics not responding to sulfonylureas: When individuals with diabetes do not respond adequately to sulfonylureas (another class of antidiabetic medication), metformin is often added as an adjunct therapy to help improve blood sugar control.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: One of the health benefits of the use of combined oral contraceptives in pre-menopausal women is that these contraceptives reduce the risk of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D) Ovarian cancer

 

  • Multiple studies have shown that the use of combined oral contraceptives is associated with a decreased risk of developing ovarian cancer. The longer the duration of use, the greater the reduction in risk. This protective effect persists for many years after discontinuing the use of oral contraceptives.
  • The other options listed are not specifically associated with a reduced risk by the use of combined oral contraceptives:
    1. Deep vein thrombosis: Combined oral contraceptives can slightly increase the risk of deep vein thrombosis.
    2. Migraine: The use of combined oral contraceptives may trigger or worsen migraine in some females.
    3. Ischemic stroke: The use of combined oral contraceptives can slightly increase the risk of ischemic stroke, particularly in women who have other risk factors such as smoking or hypertension.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A 67-year-old postmenopausal woman with a history of osteoporosis is being evaluated for potential pharmacological treatments to strengthen her bones. She has tried lifestyle modifications, including weight-bearing exercises and calcium supplements, with limited improvement. Her physician is considering various pharmacological agents to inhibit osteoclastic activity and thereby prevent further bone loss. Which of the following medications does NOT primarily act by inhibiting osteoclasts?
questions.solutionHtml:
erif">Ans. C. Teriparatide

 

Explanation of Options:

 

a) Denosumab: This is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits the RANKL (Receptor Activator for Nuclear Factor κ B Ligand), which is essential for the formation and function of osteoclasts. Thus, it inhibits osteoclast activity.

 

b) Strontium ranelate: This drug is used in the treatment of osteoporosis and works by both promoting bone formation and inhibiting bone resorption. It is thought to inhibit osteoclasts, although the exact mechanism is not well understood.

 

c) Teriparatide: This is the correct answer. Teriparatide is a recombinant form of parathyroid hormone. It is actually an anabolic (bone-building) agent that stimulates osteoblast activity, rather than inhibiting osteoclasts.

 

d) Raloxifene: This is a selective estrogen receptor modulator (SERM) that inhibits bone resorption by osteoclasts, thus serving to preserve bone mass in conditions like osteoporosis.

 

Teriparatide does not inhibit osteoclasts but stimulates osteoblasts, making it the correct answer for the drug that does not act by inhibiting osteoclasts.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A 45-year-old patient with a history of epilepsy presents to the clinic for medication review. The patient is currently taking multiple medications, including isoniazid, hydralazine, procainamide, and phenytoin, for their various medical conditions. During the discussion, the patient asks about the differences in the metabolism of these drugs. The healthcare provider explains that all the drugs mentioned are metabolized by different pathways except for one. Which of the following drugs is NOT metabolized by acetylation?
questions.solutionHtml:
"font-family:Calibri,sans-serif">Ans. D. Phenytoin

 

Explanation:

 

  • Among the drugs mentioned, phenytoin is not metabolized by acetylation. Phenytoin is primarily metabolized through hepatic oxidation, mediated by cytochrome P450 enzymes, specifically CYP2C9. It undergoes extensive hepatic metabolism rather than acetylation.
  • On the other hand, the other drugs mentioned are metabolized by acetylation:
    • Isoniazid (Choice A) is an antituberculosis medication that undergoes rapid acetylation in the liver. Acetylation plays a significant role in the metabolism of isoniazid, and variations in acetylation rates can impact its therapeutic efficacy and side effects.
    • Hydralazine (Choice B), an antihypertensive drug, is also metabolized by acetylation. Acetylation is a major pathway involved in the elimination of hydralazine from the body.
    • Procainamide (Choice C), an antiarrhythmic medication, undergoes extensive acetylation for its metabolism. Acetylation is a major metabolic pathway for procainamide, and acetylator phenotype variations can affect the drug's efficacy and potential toxicity.
    • Therefore, the drug that is NOT metabolized by acetylation among the options provided is phenytoin (Choice D). It is primarily metabolized through hepatic oxidation rather than acetylation.

questions.stem: A continuous intravenous infusion of a drug was started at a rate of 3 mg/min. The drug has a half-life of 3 hours, a volume of distribution of 120 L, and a clearance of 0.6 L/min. If the rate of infusion remains constant, what will be the plasma concentration at steady-state?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans D. 5.0 mg/L

This is a straightforward question. The most difficult aspect is to determine which values given in the stem are necessary to answer this question. The patient is given a constant intravenous infusion (maintenance dose) of a drug and the clearance is known. This is all that is necessary to determine the plasma concentration at steady state. 

The equation to use is: 

MD = CL X Cpss/ F

where, 

Cpss = plasma concentration at steady state 

CL = clearance 

F = bioavailability 

In this instance, the bioavailability is one (100%) because the drug is given intravenously, so all of the drug is "absorbed." 

So, 

Cpss = MD/CL = 3/0.6 = 5 mg/L

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A 62-year-old male patient presents to the clinic with sudden onset of weakness and numbness on the right side of his body, difficulty speaking, and a sudden severe headache. He denies any recent trauma or significant changes in his lifestyle. On physical examination, there is evidence of right-sided hemiparesis and decreased sensation. The patient's speech is slurred, and he exhibits mild confusion. His blood pressure is within normal limits, and the rest of the physical examination is unremarkable. He has a past medical history significant for a stroke that occurred 6 months ago. At that time, he was initiated on clopidogrel for secondary prevention. The patient has been compliant with his medications, including clopidogrel, since his initial stroke. Given this clinical scenario, the most probable cause for the patient's recurrent stroke despite being on clopidogrel is:
questions.solutionHtml:
man",serif">Ans B. Poor metabolism by CYP2C19

Explanation

Given this clinical scenario, the most probable cause for the patient's recurrent stroke despite being on clopidogrel is poor metabolism by CYP 2C19. Clopidogrel is a prodrug that requires hepatic activation by cytochrome P450 enzymes, primarily CYP 2C19, to form its active metabolite. This active metabolite inhibits platelet aggregation and helps prevent further clot formation in patients at risk for stroke. However, some individuals have genetic variations that result in poor metabolism of clopidogrel by CYP 2C19, leading to reduced effectiveness of the drug. This phenomenon is known as clopidogrel resistance. Patients who are poor metabolizers of clopidogrel may have a higher risk of recurrent stroke despite taking the medication as prescribed

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A young boy presents to the emergency department with constant crying due to pain after a history of bite from an insect. The patient complains of severe pain at the sting site, restlessness, sweating, and increased heart rate. On examination, the patient has local erythema and swelling at the site. The patient's blood pressure is elevated. What is the most appropriate treatment for this patient?
questions.solutionHtml:
n dir="ltr" lang="EN-IN" style="font-family:"Calibri",sans-serif">Ans.  A. Administration of prazosin

Explanation:

  • The symptoms described by the patient, including severe pain, restlessness, sweating, and increased heart rate, are consistent with scorpion envenomation. Scorpion venom can cause an excessive release of catecholamines, leading to sympathetic overactivity.
  • Prazosin acts by blocking alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, counteracting the effects of the released catecholamines.
  • Options B and C, administration of antihistamines and corticosteroids, respectively, are not the mainstays of treatment for scorpion stings. Antihistamines are primarily used for the management of allergic reactions, which are not the primary mechanism of scorpion envenomation. Corticosteroids may have a limited role in certain cases, but they are not the initial treatment of choice.
  • Option D, application of ice packs, may help provide local pain relief, but it does not address the systemic symptoms associated with scorpion envenomation.Top of Form

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A drug addict patient presented with agitation and ulceration on skin. The patient had severe itching and scratch marks on the body. On examination there is presence of tachycardia, mydriasis and hypertension. Likely substance responsible for these symptoms is?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Cocaine

  • Based on the symptoms described, including agitation, ulceration on the skin, severe itching, scratch marks on the body, tachycardia, mydriasis (pupil dilation), and hypertension, the likely substance responsible for these symptoms is Cocaine.
  • Cocaine is a powerful stimulant drug that affects the central nervous system. It is known to cause agitation, increased energy levels, and a sense of euphoria.
  • Cocaine can result in feeling of insects running on the skin, a type of tactile hallucination (formication; Magnum Phenomenon). This leads to intense itching and the compulsive behavior of scratching, which can result in skin ulceration and scratch marks.
  • Cocaine stimulates the sympathetic nervous system, leading to physiological responses such as increased heart rate (tachycardia), pupil dilation (mydriasis), and elevated blood pressure (hypertension).

In contrast:

  • Cannabis (marijuana) is not typically associated with severe itching, scratch marks, or ulceration. It may cause relaxation, euphoria, and mild dilation of the pupils, but it is not commonly associated with tachycardia or hypertension.
  • LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide) is a hallucinogenic drug that primarily affects perception and mood. It does not typically cause agitation, ulceration on the skin, severe itching, scratch marks, tachycardia, mydriasis, or hypertension.
  • Heroin is an opioid drug that generally causes sedation, respiratory depression, constricted pupils (miosis), and decreased blood pressure.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A college student is brought to emergency after taking an overdose of a non-prescription drug. The patient is confused and lethargic. He has been hyperventilating and dehydrated. Arterial blood gas analysis demonstrates metabolic acidosis. In the management of this patient, which is NOT likely to be of any therapeutic value?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. Treatment with acetyl cysteine

  • Based on the symptoms described, including confusion, lethargy, hyperventilation, dehydration, and metabolic acidosis, the most likely diagnosis for the college student who took an overdose of a non-prescription drug is salicylate (aspirin) poisoning.
  • Acetylcysteine is an antidote used for the treatment of acetaminophen (paracetamol) poisoning, not salicylate poisoning. It helps prevent liver damage caused by acetaminophen overdose by replenishing depleted glutathione stores. However, it does not have a specific role in the treatment of salicylate poisoning.
  • The appropriate interventions for managing salicylate poisoning include:
    • Alkalinization of urine: Salicylates are weak acids that can be reabsorbed in the acidic environment of the renal tubules. Alkalinization of urine can promote salicylate excretion and enhance elimination.
    • Correction of metabolic acidosis: Salicylate poisoning can lead to metabolic acidosis due to the accumulation of salicylic acid and its metabolites. Correcting metabolic acidosis is an important aspect of managing the patient.
    • Gastric lavage: In cases of severe salicylate poisoning, gastric lavage may be considered shortly after ingestion to remove any remaining unabsorbed drug. However, its utility decreases as time passes since ingestion, and it is not effective in removing already absorbed salicylates.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Individuals with alcoholic cirrhosis of liver may develop severe hepatotoxicity after doses of acetaminophen that are not toxic to individuals with normal liver function. This increase sensitivity to acetaminophen’s toxicity is due to?

options.label: C
options.text: Decreased activity of Cytochrome P450 enzymes

questions.solutionHtml:
man",serif">Ans. B. Decreased hepatocellular stores of glutathione

Explanation

  • Acetaminophen is primarily metabolized in the liver through a process that involves the formation of a toxic metabolite called N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine (NAPQI). Under normal circumstances, NAPQI is rapidly detoxified by glutathione, preventing liver damage.
  • However, individuals with alcoholic cirrhosis often have reduced levels of glutathione in their hepatocytes (liver cells). This decreased glutathione availability impairs the detoxification of NAPQI, leading to an accumulation of the toxic metabolite in the liver. Consequently, the hepatocytes are more susceptible to damage and toxicity, even with lower doses of acetaminophen that would be well-tolerated by individuals with normal liver function.
  • Factors such as decreased availability of acetaldehyde dehydrogenase (choice A), decreased activity of Cytochrome P450 enzymes (choice C), or increased liver blood flow (choice D) may contribute to liver damage in other contexts or with different substances, but they are not the primary reasons for the increased sensitivity to acetaminophen's toxicity in individuals with alcoholic cirrhosis.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A new born was diagnosed as having a congenital abnormality that resulted in transposition of great vessels. While preparing the infant for surgery, the medical team needed to keep the ducts arteriosus open. They did this by infusing?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Alprostadil

 

  • In the case of a newborn diagnosed with transposition of the great vessels, there is a need to maintain patency of the ductus arteriosus, a blood vessel that connects the pulmonary artery to the aorta.
  • Normally PGE2 keep the ductus arterious patent in intrauterine life.To keep the ductus arteriosus open in this situation, a medication called alprostadil is used. Alprostadil is a synthetic form of prostaglandin E1 (PGE1).
  • Cortisol (choice A) is a hormone involved in various physiological processes, but it is not used to keep the ductus arteriosus open in this scenario.
  • Indomethacin (choice B) is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) that is sometimes used to close a patent ductus arteriosus, rather than keep it open.
  • Tacrolimus (choice D) is an immunosuppressive drug commonly used in organ transplantation, but it is not used to maintain ductus arteriosus patency.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Which of the following is the fastest urate lowering therapy in tumor lysis syndrome to prevent renal damage?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Rasburicase

 

  • Tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) is a potentially life-threatening condition that can occur in patients undergoing chemotherapy for cancer. It is characterized by the rapid breakdown of cancer cells, leading to the release of large amounts of intracellular contents, including uric acid, into the bloodstream. The elevated levels of uric acid can cause renal damage, including acute kidney injury.
  • Rasburicase is an enzyme that catalyzes the breakdown of uric acid into a more soluble compound called allantoin, which is easily excreted by the kidneys. By rapidly reducing the levels of uric acid, rasburicase helps prevent the formation of urate crystals and subsequent renal damage.

 

Other Options:

 

Option A.  and B Allopurinol and Febuxostat: They are other commonly used urate-lowering agents, but they are not as rapid in their onset of action as rasburicase. They work by inhibiting an enzyme called xanthine oxidase, which is involved in the production of uric acid.

 

Option D. Furosemide: It is a loop diuretic and is not primarily used for urate-lowering purposes. It helps promote diuresis and may be used to enhance urine flow in TLS, but it does not directly target uric acid levels.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Which of the following is not true about use of β blockers in CHF?

options.label: A
options.text: These should be started at very low dose and slowly titrated upwards

options.label: B
options.text: Carvedilol is most widely used β blockers

options.label: C
options.text: These are drug of choice in acute decompensated heart failure

options.label: D
options.text: These can reduce mortality in CHF patient

questions.answerText: These are drug of choice in acute decompensated heart failure
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. These are drug of choice in acute decompensated heart failure

  • β blockers have shown benefits in chronic CHF but are contra-indicated in acute decompensated heart failure.
  • Options A, B, and D are true statements regarding the use of β blockers in CHF:
    • These should be started at very low doses and slowly titrated upwards: This is true because starting β blockers at low doses allows for monitoring of the patient's response and minimizing the risk of exacerbating heart failure symptoms. The dosage is then gradually increased over time as tolerated.
    • Carvedilol is the most widely used β blocker: Carvedilol is indeed one of the most commonly used β blockers in the management of CHF. It has been extensively studied in clinical trials and has shown benefits in improving cardiac function and reducing mortality.
    • These can reduce mortality in CHF patients: β blockers have been shown to improve survival and reduce mortality in patients with chronic heart failure. They help reduce the workload on the heart, improve cardiac function, and prevent further cardiac remodeling.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: In which of the following patients would enalapril be the best first line agent for high blood pressure control?

options.label: A
options.text: A 62 year old man with bilateral renal artery stenosis

options.label: C
options.text: A 41 year old woman with hyperkalemia

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. A 56 year old diabetic woman

  • Enalapril is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor commonly used as a first-line agent for high blood pressure control. It works by blocking the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, a potent vasoconstrictor, leading to vasodilation and lowering of blood pressure.
  • In patients with diabetes, hypertension is a common coexisting condition, and ACE inhibitors have demonstrated renal-protective effects, reducing proteinuria and slowing the progression of diabetic kidney disease. ACE inhibitors are also considered favorable in patients with diabetes due to their potential cardioprotective effects.
  • Options A, B, and C are actually contra-indications of ACE inhibitors. 
    • A 62-year-old man with bilateral renal artery stenosis: In patients with bilateral renal artery stenosis, ACE inhibitors are generally avoided as they can cause renal impairment and potentially worsen the stenosis.
    • A 32-year-old pregnant female: ACE inhibitors, including enalapril, are contraindicated during pregnancy due to their potential risks to fetal development.
    • A 41-year-old woman with hyperkalemia: ACE inhibitors, including enalapril, can cause an increase in potassium levels. Therefore, in patients with pre-existing hyperkalemia, ACE inhibitors may not be the best choice as they can further elevate potassium levels and potentially lead to complications.


ore, in patients with pre-existing hyperkalemia, ACE inhibitors may not be the best choice as they can further elevate potassium levels and potentially lead to complications.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Which of these drugs DO NOT decrease angiotensin II activity:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Nesiritide

  • Angiotensin II is a potent vasoconstrictor and plays a significant role in regulating blood pressure. Several medications are used to decrease the activity of angiotensin II, but nesiritide is not one of them.
  • Enalapril (choice A) is an angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitor that blocks the conversion of angiotensin I to angiotensin II, thus reducing its activity.
  • Valsartan (choice B) is an angiotensin II receptor blocker (ARB) that specifically blocks the angiotensin II type 1 (AT1) receptor, preventing the binding of angiotensin II and reducing its effects.
  • Omapatrilat (choice D) is a vasopeptidase inhibitor that inhibits both ACE and neutral endopeptidase (NEP), leading to decreased angiotensin II activity.
  • Nesiritide (choice C) is a medication used for the treatment of acute decompensated heart failure. It is a recombinant form of human B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) that primarily acts as a vasodilator and diuretic.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Which of the following hyperpolarizes AV nodal tissue, used in PSVT and has short lasting adverse effects?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Adenosine

  • Adenosine is an antiarrhythmic medication that works by activating adenosine receptors in the heart. It hyperpolarizes the AV nodal tissue, which slows down conduction through the AV node and interrupts reentrant pathways that may be causing PSVT. This helps restore normal sinus rhythm.
  • Adenosine is administered intravenously as a rapid bolus injection due to its very short half-life (less than 10 seconds). Its effects are transient, typically lasting only a few seconds to minutes. It is DOC for the acute termination of PSVT episodes.
  • Verapamil (choice A) is a calcium channel blocker that can also be used to treat PSVT, but it primarily works by blocking calcium channels to reduce the conduction through the AV node. It does not have the same hyperpolarizing effect as adenosine.
  • Digoxin (choice B) is a cardiac glycoside that is used for various cardiac conditions, including heart failure and atrial fibrillation. While it can affect AV nodal conduction, it does not have the same rapid and transient effect as adenosine.
  • Propranolol (choice D) is a beta-blocker that primarily works by blocking beta-adrenergic receptors. While it can slow down heart rate, it does not have the same hyperpolarizing effect on AV nodal tissue as adenosine.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Which of the following drug can decrease bone resorption as well as increase bone formation?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B) Romosozumab

 

  • Romosozumab is the drug that can decrease bone resorption as well as increase bone formation. It is a monoclonal antibody that works by inhibiting sclerostin, a protein that suppresses bone formation. By blocking sclerostin, romosozumab promotes bone formation (by stimulating osteoblasts) and simultaneously decreases bone resorption (by inhibiting osteoclasts), resulting in increased bone density and strength.
  • Denosumab (choice a) is a medication that primarily inhibits bone resorption. It is a monoclonal antibody that targets and blocks receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa-B ligand (RANKL), a protein involved in the formation, function, and survival of osteoclasts. By inhibiting RANKL, denosumab reduces bone resorption.
  • Teriparatide (choice c) is a recombinant form of parathyroid hormone (PTH) that stimulates bone formation but does not have a direct effect on bone resorption.
  • Cinacalcet (choice d) is a medication used to treat hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia by modulating the activity of the parathyroid hormone (PTH) and calcium-sensing receptors.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A professor in medical college is teaching students about the adverse effects of a drug. Which of the following drug can cause gynaecomastia in men and menstrual irregularities in women?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Spironolactone

  • Spironolactone is a medication that belongs to the class of aldosterone receptor antagonists. It is commonly used as a diuretic and also has antiandrogenic properties. Due to its antiandrogenic effects, spironolactone can interfere with the action of androgens (male hormones) and lead to hormonal imbalances.
  • In men, spironolactone can cause gynecomastia, which is the development of breast tissue. This is because spironolactone can block the androgen receptors and inhibit the effects of testosterone.
  • In women, spironolactone can cause menstrual irregularities. It may lead to changes in the menstrual cycle, including irregular periods or changes in the flow.

Drugs causing gynaecomastia:

DI:        Digoxin

S:         Spironolactone

C:         Cimetidine

K:         Ketoconazole

O:        Oestrogens

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: At a high altitude of 3000m, a person complains of breathlessness. All of the following can be used for management of this person except?
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. Intravenous digoxin

  • Intravenous digoxin is not a suitable choice for managing breathlessness at high altitude. Digoxin is a medication primarily used for the treatment of heart failure and certain arrhythmias. It works by increasing the strength of heart contractions. However, its mechanism of action does not address the specific challenges associated with high altitude-related breathlessness.
  • The other options listed are all potential management strategies for breathlessness at high altitude:
    • Oxygen supplementation: Providing supplemental oxygen can help alleviate breathlessness and improve oxygenation at high altitudes, where the air is thinner and contains less oxygen. Oxygen supplementation can help relieve symptoms and improve overall well-being.
    • Immediate descent: Descending to a lower altitude is often the most effective way to alleviate breathlessness and symptoms associated with altitude sickness. Descending allows for a greater concentration of oxygen in the air, reducing the strain on the respiratory system.
    • Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide is a medication commonly used for the prevention and treatment of altitude sickness. It works by increasing the excretion of bicarbonate, which helps alleviate symptoms associated with high altitude, including breathlessness.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: Mannitol is used in the management of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. B. Acute Congestive Glaucoma

  • Acute congestive glaucoma is a condition characterized by a sudden increase in intraocular pressure due to impaired fluid drainage in the eye. Mannitol is administered intravenously in this condition as an osmotic diuretic to rapidly reduce intraocular pressure. It works by drawing fluid out of the eye, thereby relieving the pressure and preventing further damage to the optic nerve.
  • The other options listed are not the contra-indications of mannitol:
      • Congestive Cardiac Failure: While diuretics may be used in the management of congestive heart failure, mannitol can worsen this condition by increasing intravascular volume due to its osmotic effect.
      • Acute Renal Failure: Mannitol can be used in impending renal failure but is contra-indicated in acute renal failure.
      • Pulmonary Edema: Mannitol can worsen this condition by increasing intravascular volume due to its osmotic effect.

questions.stem: Which of the following patients is most likely to be treated with intravenous glucagon?

options.label: A
options.text: A young man who took cocaine and has a blood pressure of 190/110 mm Hg

options.label: B
options.text: A middle aged man with type II diabetes who has not taken his regular dose of glipizide for last 4 days

options.label: C
options.text: An old woman with lactic acidosis as a complication of severe infection and shock

options.label: D
options.text: An old man with severe bradycardia and hypotension resulting from ingestion of overdose of atenolol

questions.answerText: An old man with severe bradycardia and hypotension resulting from ingestion of overdose of atenolol
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. D. An old man with severe bradycardia and hypotension resulting from ingestion of overdose of atenolol

  • In cases of beta-blocker (e.g., atenolol) poisoning, glucagon can be administered to counteract the effects of beta-blockers and increase cardiac output. The mechanism of action of glucagon in beta blocker poisoning involves bypassing the blocked beta-adrenergic receptors and stimulating other signaling pathways to enhance cardiac function.
  • When beta-blockers block beta-adrenergic receptors, they inhibit the normal sympathetic response mediated by beta-adrenergic stimulation. This can result in decreased heart rate, reduced contractility, and vasodilation, leading to hypotension and decreased cardiac output.
  • Glucagon, on the other hand, acts by binding to specific glucagon receptors in the heart and blood vessels. Its mechanism of action in beta blocker poisoning involves the following:
    • Activation of adenylate cyclase: Glucagon binding to its receptors activates adenylate cyclase, which leads to the production of cyclic adenosine monophosphate (cAMP). This bypasses the blocked beta-adrenergic receptors and stimulates intracellular signaling pathways independent of beta-adrenergic receptors.
    • Increased intracellular calcium levels: The activation of adenylate cyclase by glucagon results in increased intracellular levels of cAMP. This, in turn, promotes the release of calcium from intracellular stores, leading to an increase in intracellular calcium levels. Increased calcium levels enhance myocardial contractility, resulting in improved cardiac output.
  • The other options listed are less likely to be treated with intravenous glucagon.

questions.topic: Cerebellum · 023-Pharmacology E&D Part-1, Mission 3.0 (Early Intern Batch) - 12-05-2025 - 2025-05-12
questions.stem: A 54-year old obese patient with type 2 diabetes mellitus and a history of alcoholism probably should not receive metformin because it can increase the risk of:
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C. Lactic acidosis

 

  • Metformin is an oral medication commonly used to treat type 2 diabetes. It works by reducing glucose production in the liver, improving insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues, and reducing glucose absorption in the intestines. While it is generally considered safe and effective, there are certain conditions and situations where metformin should be used with caution or avoided.
  • One such condition is alcoholism, as alcohol can impair liver function and increase the risk of lactic acidosis. Lactic acidosis is a rare but serious condition characterized by the buildup of lactic acid in the blood. Metformin use in individuals with compromised liver function, such as those with alcoholism or liver disease, can further increase the risk of lactic acidosis.
  • The other options listed are not directly associated with metformin use:

 

A. Disulfiram-like reaction: A disulfiram-like reaction is a side effect that can occur with certain medications when combined with alcohol consumption. It is not directly associated with metformin use.

 

B. Hypoglycemia: Metformin can lower blood sugar levels in diabetics but it is not associated with an increased risk of hypoglycemia.

 

D. Severe hepatic toxicity: Metformin is generally well-tolerated and does not typically cause severe hepatic toxicity.

questions.stem: All of the statements about liraglutide are FALSE except:

options.label: B
options.text: It is an amylin analog useful in diabetes mellitus

options.label: D
options.text: It can be used for treatment of type 1 as well as type 2 diabetes mellitus

questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. A. It acts by releasing insulin

 

  • Liraglutide is a medication used in the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus. It belongs to the class of drugs known as glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists. Liraglutide works by mimicking the actions of the natural hormone GLP-1, which is released in response to food intake. Endogenous GLP-1 leads to release of insulin and thus prevents rise in blood sugar after meals. The same is done by liraglutide.
    • It is an amylin analog useful in diabetes mellitus: This statement is false. Liraglutide is not an amylin analog. It is a GLP-1 receptor agonist and has different mechanisms of action compared to amylin analogs.
    • It is effective orally: Liraglutide is not effective orally. It is administered once daily via subcutaneous injection.
    • It can be used for the treatment of type 1 as well as type 2 diabetes mellitus: This statement is false. Liraglutide is indicated for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus. It is not approved for use in type 1 diabetes mellitus.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about dapagliflozin is true?

options.label: A
options.text: Its major mode of action in diabetes mellitus is to cause glucosuria when serum glucose is above 180 mg/dL.

options.label: B
options.text: It acts by inhibiting SGLT2 present in collecting tubules of the nephron

options.label: C
options.text: Urinary tract infections are common with its use

questions.answerText: Urinary tract infections are common with its use
questions.solutionHtml:
Ans. C) Urinary tract infections are common with its use

 

  • Dapagliflozin is a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitor. Let's evaluate each statement:
    • Dapagliflozin does increase glucosuria (excretion of glucose in the urine), but it doesn't only work when blood glucose levels are above 180 mg/dL. It promotes glucosuria by inhibiting the reabsorption of glucose in the kidneys, which occurs regardless of blood glucose levels. Renal threshold for glucose is 180 mg/dL and glucosuria occurs even without dapagliflozin when blood sugar is above this value.
    • Dapagliflozin acts by inhibiting SGLT2, but these transporters are located primarily in the proximal convoluted tubule of the nephron, not the collecting tubules. SGLT2 transporters are responsible for the majority of the reabsorption of filtered glucose back into the bloodstream.
    • There is a slightly increased risk of urinary tract infections (UTIs) with SGLT2 inhibitors like dapagliflozin, as the increased glucose in the urine can promote bacterial growth.
